label: copy-phase c/w input right after a v (sparse conjunction)
predicate: (phase == 2) & isin(in_tok, [tok("c"), tok("w")]) & (prev_tok == tok("v")) & isin(out_tok, [tok("w"), tok("d"), tok("c"), tok("u"), tok("q"), tok("o")])
explanation: Very sparse (0.01% of steps). 98% of mass is in the copy phase, nearly always on a repeated input (in_first=0). The input is c or w in 80% of mass (d, o make up most of the rest), and the previous input is v in 65% of mass. Top activations are the pattern ... v [c|w] in the copy phase, with the output (next original token) usually w/d/c/u/q/o. Density rises toward the end of the copy (high recall_idx, to_go 0-1). Still, the feature fires on only a small fraction of the steps that match these conditions: copy-phase c/w gives mass recall 0.80 at precision 0.003, and the best conjunction (v then c/w with an output from {w,d,c,u,q,o}) gets F1 of about 0.27 on dev. So the token context is clear but what actually decides when it fires is not captured. It does not fire during the original phase (except a few t>=4 cases), on the delimiter step, or on digit inputs.
